t: This is Youth, a figurative sculpture standing about nine feet, or 2.7 metres, tall. Daphne Hardy Henrion made it, and she modelled it on a full-size cast of her own body. The architect Leonard Manasseh commissioned it, and it was first shown at the Festival of Britain in 1951. Henrion was a British sculptor and a friend of the writer Arthur Koestler. She wanted the figure to be a graceful and friendly personality, and you can judge for yourself whether it is.
